newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault says Vilvoorde closure irrevocable.
newsitem.headline: Renault says Vilvoorde closure irrevocable.

text.p: Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer reiterated on Wednesday after meeting Belgian union leaders that the French carmaker's decision to close the Vilvoorde assembly plant in Belgium was irrevocable.
"I confirmed that this decision was irrevocable," Schweitzer told reporters at the end of a two and a half hour meeting with union leaders that was held in this northern French town.

Schweitzer said they discussed resumption of operations, which have been halted at the plant since February 27 when the company announced plans to shut it down. The two sides also discussed measures to accompany the closure, such as internal transfers.

Schweitzer said Renault was willing to hold more talks on these issues without setting pre-conditions. The chairman, who left the site before the union representatives, was surrounded by security guards as he made his brief statement.

Schweitzer and about 10 union officials had agreed to meet on "neutral ground" in Beauvais, a northern French city roughly midway between Renault's Paris headquarters and the plant at Vilvoorde which Renault has said it will shut down by July 27.
Renault's decision to close the plant has triggered outrage across Europe but particularly in Belgium where trade unions denounced the shock announcement as "unbelievably brutal".
